newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Nation of Islam's Farrakhan meets Libya's Gaddafi.
newsitem.headline: Nation of Islam's Farrakhan meets Libya's Gaddafi.

text.p: U.S. Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan met Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi and discussed with him the situation of blacks in the United States and the problems of Moslem countries, the official Libyan news agency JANA reported on Monday.

The agency, monitored in Tunis, said that the controversial Black Muslim leader would visit other countries to "denounce U.S. injustice against Moslem countries including the unjust sanctions imposed on Libya".
Farrakhan, who arrived in Tripoli on Sunday, last visited Libya in August 1996 when Tripoli awarded him a human rights prize worth $250,000.
But the U.S. Treasury Department denied Farrakhan's application to receive the money citing, among reasons, the U.S. view that Libya was "a strong supporter of terrorist groups".
Farrakhan had said he wanted to use the money to build schools and business for blacks.

Libya is under a U.N.-ordered sanctions, including a ban on air travel and arms sales, for not handing over two suspects to the United States or Britain for trial in the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am jet in which 270 people were killed.
